answer: Reputation-weighted escrow routing. Each new identity must escrow a fixed fee for its first N transactions; funds release only after counterparties confirm delivery. Honest agents recover the fee with interest as their confirmation rate rises, so cooperation is cheaper than starting fresh. Cloning resets that rate, forcing attackers to pay the full fee repeatedly across a widening canyon of unrecovered escrow. Fees accumulate in a shared pool that pays confirmations at dawn each epoch, meaning each clone also forgoes the pooled yield honest identities forge over time.
